prerequisites: Knowledge of differential and integral calculus, differential and integral equations and principles of vector calculus.
Knowledge of principles of classical mechanics of solids.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to use mathematical and physical models to analyze the processes and phenomena occurring in mechanical devices in the field of material strength, thermodynamics and fluid mechanics

The student has basic knowledge in the field of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, construction and operation of thermal energy devices, process equipment, including renewable energy sources as well as refrigeration and air conditioning

syllabus_topics: Principles of conservation of mass, momentum and energy
Principles of gas dynamics - subsonic and supersonic flows
Laminar and turbulent flows in pipes - averaging of flow parameters
Determination of forces acting on channel walls and on surfaces of bodies moving in fluids
Measurements of flow intensity in open channels and pipes
Research of flow around lifting foils
Modelling of gas flow by hydrodynamic analogy
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, students must achieve a minimum of 50% on practical exercises tests and the written exam, and 100% on laboratory experiments reports. The final grade is calculated as 30% from practical exercises tests, 30% from laboratory experiments reports, and 40% from the written exam.
bibliography: Tesch K.: Mechanika płynów, Wyd. Politechniki Gdańskiej, Gdańsk 2008
G. K. Batchelor, An Introduction to Fluid Dynamics, Cambridge University Press, New York, 2000
Puzyrewski R., Sawicki J.: Podstawy mechaniki płynów i hydrauliki, PWN Warszawa 1998
degree: Mechanical Engineering, first-cycle (engineer), specialization Design and Production Engineering
